entities.summary:
Priscian of Lydia, a prominent figure in the twilight of classical antiquity, stands as one of the final exponents of the Neoplatonic school, active in the tumultuous 6th century CE. Hailing from Lydia in Asia Minor, his intellectual journey likely took him to the vibrant philosophical centers of Athens and Alexandria before the definitive closure of the Athenian Academy in 529 CE by Emperor Justinian I. His significance lies in representing the intellectual resilience of pagan philosophy amidst the ascendance of Christian dogma, offering a rare glimpse into the sophisticated arguments and methods of late antique Platonism as it faced its demise.

Priscian's scholarly contributions are primarily preserved in two surviving works: the *Solutiones ad Chosroem* and *De theologicis quaestionibus*. The *Solutiones*, a series of answers to philosophical questions posed by the Persian King Khosrow I Anushirvan, covers a wide range of topics from cosmology and metaphysics to psychology, demonstrating a profound engagement with both Platonic and Aristotelian thought. The *De theologicis quaestionibus*, often attributed to him, further explores complex philosophical issues, reflecting the syncretic nature of late Neoplatonism which sought to harmonize diverse ancient traditions. These texts reveal his adherence to the tenets of Iamblichus and Proclus, emphasizing emanation theory and the hierarchical structure of reality.
